sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **A full reindex now clears the rows left by content the index never saw leave.** An object leaves the index through the sync hooks, and content changed around them — a direct SQL delete, a table restored from a dump, an importer that empties a catalogue by query — never reaches them. Nothing collected what stayed behind either: a reindex walks what is publishable *now*, so it never visits an ID outside that set, and the rows lived for the life of the site. Measured on a 12 400-product shop whose catalogue had been dropped by SQL and re-imported: 12 902 dead objects, 172 118 rows — 51.5% of the table and about half its 96 MB; the test site carried 782 of its own. Such a row never reaches a result, because the ranking query joins the posts table on the same conditions and the join drops it, but it is read before that happens and it skews the weighting: the document count behind IDF comes from the same table, and on that shop it read 25 300 against 12 398 real products, with per-term frequencies inflated about twofold. A reindex now starts by dropping exactly the three states its own pass cannot visit — the post is gone, it is not published, its type is no longer covered — in small chunks so the statement stays interruptible on a table carrying hundreds of thousands of dead rows. The rest of indexability is still decided per post, unchanged.
  • **The index status now reports drift in both directions.** It warned only when the index held far fewer items than the site publishes, so the opposite case — an index holding *more* items than exist — passed in silence, which is precisely the shape the problem above takes. Exclusions can only keep a healthy index under the published count and never over it, so any excess is stale and is now named, with the count and what to do about it.
